# Session Overview

{{< include /program/_session6.md >}}

## Session Objectives

This session explores comprehensive publishing strategies for Quarto projects, covering multiple deployment platforms, automation workflows, and best practices for different use cases.

## Learning Objectives

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

By the end of this session, participants will be able to:

:::

- [Choose the right publishing method for your use case.]{.fragment fragment-index="2"}
- [Deploy a Quarto project to multiple platforms.]{.fragment fragment-index="3"}
- [Set up automated publishing workflows.]{.fragment fragment-index="4"}
- [Troubleshoot common publishing issues.]{.fragment fragment-index="5"}
- [Configure custom domains and advanced features.]{.fragment fragment-index="6"}
- [Distribute extensions via GitHub or archives.]{.fragment fragment-index="7"}

# Quarto Publishing

## Publishing Options Overview {.smaller}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

| Service            | Best For                        | Key Features                    |
|--------------------|---------------------------------|---------------------------------|
| **Quarto Pub**     | Public content, getting started | Free, simple, 100MB limit       |
| **GitHub Pages**   | Open source projects            | Git integration, custom domains |
| **Netlify**        | Professional sites              | Advanced features, previews     |
| **Posit Connect**  | Enterprise/organisations        | Security, authentication        |
| **Other Services** | Custom requirements             | Firebase, S3, self-hosted       |

:::

::: {.callout-tip .fragment fragment-index="2"}

## Rule of thumb

Start with Quarto Pub for learning, use GitHub Pages for projects, Netlify for production sites

:::

# Quarto Pub

## Your First Quarto Pub Deployment

::: {layout-ncol="2"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

1. Create an account.  
   Visit [quartopub.com](https://quartopub.com) and sign up.

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

2. Publish from CLI.
  
   ```{.bash}
   quarto publish quarto-pub
   ```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}

3. Authenticate.

   - Browser opens for authorization
   - Confirm publishing permissions
   - Site deploys automatically!

:::

::: {.callout-note .fragment fragment-index="4"}

## That's it!

Your site is live at `https://username.quarto.pub/project-name`.

:::

:::

## Understanding `_publish.yml`

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

Created automatically when you first publish:

```{.yaml filename="_publish.yml"}
- source: project
  quarto-pub:
    - id: "abc123-def456-ghi789"
      url: "https://myusername.quarto.pub/myproject"
```

:::

- [**Safe for version control** (no credentials).]{.fragment fragment-index="2"}
- [**Shareable** across team members.]{.fragment fragment-index="3"}
- [**Service configuration** stored locally.]{.fragment fragment-index="4"}
- [**Reusable** for subsequent deployments.]{.fragment fragment-index="5"}

# GitHub Pages

## Three Ways to Use GitHub Pages

::: {layout="[[0.5,0.5],[-0.25,0.5,-0.25]]"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

### Render to `docs/`

- Simplest approach
- Commit rendered output
- Good for small projects

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

### `quarto publish`

- Local rendering
- Automatic deployment
- Clean separation

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}

### GitHub Actions

- Fully automated
- Triggered by commits
- Most professional

:::

:::

## Method 1: Render to `docs/` {.smaller}

::: {layout-ncol="2"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

- Configure Output Directory

  ```yaml
  # _quarto.yml
  project:
    type: website
    output-dir: docs
  ```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

- Add `.nojekyll` File

  ```bash
  touch .nojekyll
  ```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}

- Render and Push

  ```bash
  quarto render
  git add .
  git commit -m "feat: Add rendered site"
  git push
  ```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="4"}

- Configure Repository

  Settings → Pages → Source: **Deploy from branch** → Branch: **main** → Folder: **/docs**

:::

:::

## Method 2: `quarto publish gh-pages` {.smaller}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

- Setup Source Branch

  ```bash
  # Create gh-pages branch
  git checkout --orphan gh-pages
  git rm -rf .
  git commit --allow-empty -m "chore: Initial gh-pages commit"
  git push origin gh-pages
  git checkout main
  ```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

- Configure .gitignore

  ```txt
  _site/
  _book/
  ```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}

- Publish

  ```bash
  quarto publish gh-pages
  ```

:::

## Method 3: GitHub Actions Workflow {.smaller}

- Create Workflow File: `.github/workflows/publish.yml`.

  ```yaml
  name: Quarto Publish
  on:
    workflow_dispatch:
    push:
      branches: main
  
  jobs:
    build-deploy:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      permissions:
        contents: write
      steps:
        - name: Check out repository
          uses: actions/checkout@v4
        
        - name: Set up Quarto
          uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2
        
        - name: Render and Publish
          uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/publish@v2
          with:
            target: gh-pages
          env:
            GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  ```

# Code Execution Strategies

## The Big Decision: Where to Execute Code? {.smaller}

::: {layout-ncol="2"}

::: {#execute-1 .fragment fragment-index="1"}

### Local Execution + Freeze

```{.yaml filename="_quarto.yml"}
execute:
  freeze: auto
```

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

**Pros:**

- Faster CI builds.
- Consistent environment.
- Handle legacy code.

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}

**Cons:**

- Manual re-execution needed.
- Larger repository size.

:::

:::

::: {#execute-2 .fragment fragment-index="4"}

### CI Execution

::: {.fragment fragment-index="5"}

**Pros:**

- Always fresh execution.
- Smaller repositories.
- Reproducible environments.

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="6"}

**Cons:**

- Longer build times.
- Dependency management.
- Potential CI failures.

:::

:::

:::

## Freeze Strategy Implementation {.smaller}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

- Enable Freezing

  ```{.yaml filename="_quarto.yml"}
  execute:
    freeze: auto
  ```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

- Re-render Locally

  ```bash
  quarto render
  ```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}

- Version Control

  ```bash
  git add _freeze/
  git commit -m "chore: Update frozen computations"
  git push
  ```

:::

::: {.callout-important .fragment fragment-index="4"}

The `_freeze/` directory stores computational results and **must** be committed to Git.

:::

## CI Execution with Dependencies

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Python/Jupyter Example {{< iconify fa7-brands:python >}}

```yaml
- name: Install Python and Dependencies
  uses: actions/setup-python@v5
  with:
    python-version: '3.13'
    cache: 'pip'

- name: Install Jupyter
  run: pip install jupyter

- name: Install Requirements
  run: pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### R/Knitr Example {{< iconify fa7-brands:r-project >}}

```yaml
- name: Install R
  uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
  with:
    r-version: '4.5.0'

- name: Install R Dependencies
  uses: r-lib/actions/setup-renv@v2
  with:
    cache-version: 1
```

:::

## Version Control Strategies {.smaller}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

Use a freeze strategy (*recommended*):

```yaml
execute:
  freeze: auto
```

:::

::: {layout-ncol="2" style="margin-top: 1em;"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

**Commit to Git:**

- Source files (`.qmd`).
- `_freeze/` directory.
- Configuration files.

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}

**Don't Commit:**

- `_site/`, `_book/`, or `_manuscript/`.
- Temporary files.
- Local dependencies.

:::

:::

## Environment Management

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

Use a tool to manage your R {{< iconify fa7-brands:r-project >}}, Python {{< iconify fa7-brands:python >}}, or Julia {{< iconify simple-icons:julia >}} environment:

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

- `renv` for R.
- `uv`, `pip`, or `conda` for Python.
- `Pkg` for Julia.

:::

# Advanced Topics

## Custom Domains

::: {.panel-tabset}

### GitHub Pages Custom Domain

1. Add `CNAME` file to project root:

   ```txt
   yourdomain.com
   ```

2. Configure DNS records:
   - **Apex domain:** A records to GitHub IPs.
   - **Subdomain:** CNAME to `username.github.io`.

3. Enable in repository settings.

### Netlify Custom Domain

- Automatic HTTPS.
- Easy DNS management.
- Domain purchasing available.

:::

# Extension Distribution

## Distribution Methods

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

### GitHub Distribution (Recommended)

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

```bash
# Users install with:
quarto add yourorg/company-report

# Or specific version/tag:
quarto add yourorg/company-report@v1.0.0

# Or from branch:
quarto add yourorg/company-report@main
```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}

**Benefits**: Version control, easy updates, namespace management (`yourorg/extension`).

:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}

## Distribution Methods

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

### Archive Distribution

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

```bash
# From URL:
quarto add https://example.com/company-report.zip

# From local file:
quarto add ./company-report.tar.gz
```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}

**Benefits**: No GitHub required, works offline, controlled distribution.

:::

## Publishing Best Practices

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

**Prepare your extension:**

:::

1. [**Add README.md** - Installation instructions and documentation.]{.fragment fragment-index="2"}
2. [**Include LICENSE** - Specify usage terms.]{.fragment fragment-index="3"}
3. [**Create example.qmd** - Demonstrate usage.]{.fragment fragment-index="4"}
4. [**Version with tags** - Use semantic versioning (*e.g.*, `v1.0.0`).]{.fragment fragment-index="5"}

::: {.callout-tip .fragment fragment-index="6"}

See [Distributing Extensions](https://quarto.org/docs/extensions/distributing.html) for complete details.

:::
